page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.9 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers. The Intel Xeon CPU achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1125.48 and a multi-core score of 2941.66, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.49 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect limited throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 18.99 GB/sec and a Passmark CPU encryption score of 1338.88.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1, this instance presents a clear tradeoff, offering dedicated compute resources but highly constrained memory capacity. This profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints, avoiding the expense of unneeded RAM. It is suited for lightweight batch processing, basic web serving, and simple database operations, but is poorly suited for memory-intensive applications or large language model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, this instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading and a 45 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or GPU resources. Benchmark results place its performance in the lower quartiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 926.0 and multi-core score of 1979.0. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1 GB per vCPU makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for CPU-bound tasks with minimal memory requirements. It is best suited for lightweight batch processing, basic static web serving, and simple database operations.
